chunks: Muhammad ibn Muyassir narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام would not return a bondwoman because of a defect once she had been intimately used, but he would recover compensation equal to the value of the defect.
And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “I seek refuge in Allah from making for her a payment.”

key_terms.بِعَيْبٍ: because of a defect or flaw affecting the sale
key_terms.بِقِيمَةِ ٱلْعَيْبِ: with compensation equal to the assessed value of the defect
key_terms.مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ: an expression of seeking refuge in Allah
key_terms.ٱلْجَارِيَةَ: a bondwoman or female slave in the context of sale law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bondwoman is found defective after she has been intimate with?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a bondwoman purchased with a defect: if she has already been intimate with, she is not returned, but compensation is taken for the defect's value. It also preserves a statement of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام expressing aversion to treating such intimacy as something warranting a compensatory wage.
